Aardvark Sensing provides an autonomous robotic ecosystem designed for large-scale and long-running soil surveys. Our durable robots operate continuously for extended periods without human intervention, conducting systematic scans of agricultural land with navigational accuracy at the centimeter level and a continuous connection to the cloud.
Carrying various sensing payloads on board, including spectrometers, cosmic ray neutron detectors, acoustic sonar, ground-penetrating radar and more, each robot gathers essential data on soil characteristics. These measurements include surface roughness, soil compaction, soil moisture, mineral content, nutrient levels, sub-surface soil structure, and more.
Our primary goals are to improve soil classification models derived from Sentinel data and enhance the resolution of soil moisture assessments from SMOS satellites. By providing ground truth data to improve satellite data application, we leverage the vast availability of satellite data.
We offer our ecosystem as a research tool to research institutes, enabling systematic soil research. By exploring the research community, we constantly discover new potential applications and needs, such as levee integrity monitoring through ground-penetrating radar, the quantifying of soil quality and pollutants for compliance with the EU Green Deal, and peacetime landmine clearance

description: Imagine you could analyze every place on earth every day from the stratosphere or lower with a reusable device carried by the wind and solar energy. Imagine internet and communication possibilities all over the world at far lower costs and space debris compared to today’s satellites. Imagine economically friendly UAVs that fulfil those long missions, which today have to be done by manned aerial carriers, like helicopters or planes, like the analysis of large areas e.g. for agriculture, resource exploration surveys, forestry and many more. These are the challenges we started to tackle. The h-aero® flight system combines the established flight concepts: airplane, helicopter and balloon. With solar cells on and under the large hull, it can fulfil 24h and autonomous flight-missions. In case of an emergency, the structure acts like a parachute. The hull is filled with helium and ensures natural buoyancy. At the same time the hull provides a comparable aerodynamic behaviour as a Frisbee. The technical description can be read in the patent documents DE102006028885A1 and PCT EP2017/063221. Our first carriers are made to harvest the "low hanging fruits" of this technology and to raise social acceptance. At the same time we tought it to fly autonomous.

entityDescription:
The research carried out in the Centre is of an interdisciplinary character and covers a wide range of topics related with such areas of science as chemistry, physics, biology and medicine. The main aim of the research is to develop novel polymers, carbon-polymer materials, carbon materials and to examine their properties so as to utilize them in biotechnology, microtechnology, optoelectronics, protection of the environment and healthcare.
The currently performed studies comprise the following issues:
- Materials to be used in biology, biochemistry and healthcare:- polymers reacting to stimuli from the environment for controlled release of biologically active materials
- carbon materials for oxygen biosensors
- thermo responding substrates for growing cell sheets
- polymeric resorbable surgical systems with shape memory
- polymers and oligomers of 3-hydroxybutyric acid to be used in medicine
- polymer systems for the controlled drug release - influence of the drug on the hydrolytic degradation of polymers

- Materials for the protection of the environment:- polymers for packaging undergoing organic recycling, including cosmetic industry packaging
- polymer and polymer-inorganic hybrid membrane materials for gas and liquid separations
- novel catalytic materials to improve the properties of diesel fuels by removal of organic sulphur compounds
- new catalysts for reduction of nitrogen oxides emission from flue gases

- Construction materials:- systems based on epoxy and cyanate ester resins
- core-shell nanoparticles utilized as polyester resin fillers
- biomorphous composites prepared using monolithic porous carbon supports derived from carbonised vascular plants and selected polymers, e.g. chitosan and poly(furfuryl alcohol)
- carbonaceous materials derived from blends of coals and selected porous carbon materials
- nano carbon tubes and fibers used as catalysts and composite material fillers

- Materials for electronics and optoelectronics:- polymer-semiconductor hybrid layer structures
- luminescent polymers
- polymer materials for photovoltaic cells

- Methods and techniques of structural research:- utilization of novel methods of high resolution nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy (NMR) in structural analysis of biodegradable copolymers
- microstructure studies of macromolecular chains by means of NMR spectroscopy (acrylate - methylacrylate copolymers)
- structural studies of biodegradable copolymers using mass spectrometry and soft ionization techniques
- properties of linear and nonlinear macromolecules in solutions, and methods of their characterization

- Magnetic Levitation (Maglev): Zeleros utilizes magnetic levitation to suspend the hyperloop pods above the track, eliminating friction and allowing for smooth, efficient movement. This technology relies on powerful magnets and high-performance non-linear control algorithms to lift and propel the pods, reducing energy consumption and enabling high-speed travel.

- Propulsion: Zeleros employs electric drivetrains and batteries to propel the hyperloop pods forward along the track. Zeleros ensures safety and tailored solutions for an efficient acceleration, essential for achieving the rapid speeds characteristic of hyperloop travel.

Zeleros' propulsion technologies are designed to optimize energy efficiency, minimize environmental impact, and ensure passenger safety. Through continuous research, development, and testing, Zeleros is advancing the feasibility and scalability of hyperloop transportation, positioning itself as a key player in the future of high-speed, sustainable travel.

description: Azulfy provides accurate measurements and reports about water, air and soil pollution for any location in the world and in any date, using Space and Local readings. Azulfy delivers environmental pollution analysis (both in real-time and historical) to help public services and tourism platforms to accurately gauge the level of pollution in the ocean, rivers, beaches and atmosphere at a given coordinate.
entityDescription:
Azulfy (formerly known as Green Travel Spots and GTS Space Technologies) was the winner of the Portuguese edition of the 3rd Cassini Hackathon, and second place in the European Cassini Competition. Azulfy uses space technology – namely Earth Observation – to perform pollution analytics and assessments over machine learning algorithms. Through the analysis of Satellite Images, we aim to monitor several pollution indicators from water, air and soil, providing reliable alerts to local governments and policy makers – our main clients. The indicators monitored by Azulfy were defined by the EU2030 goals and also feedback from potential clients.
The problem identified by Azulfy, still during the Cassini Hackathon, was that the methods for pollution monitoring by local municipalities were too manual, depending on the skills of the staff allocated to the department of the Environment. In that sense, when a pollution issue or disaster occurs, governments do not have adequate tools to monitor the impact of these events or evaluate damage, while also using unofficial multiple sources of information that makes it impossible to drive intelligent decisions.
Azulfy covers these issues through its Pollution Crisis Management System, a SaaS platform that provides daily status of several pollution variables. In addition, our platform provides automatic alerts when a certain variable level is above threshold, allowing an instant reaction from local governments. Currently, the monitoring of pollutions variables is made through laboratory analysis, which may take up to 15 days to present results. Azulfy’s platform also creates a chat channel for each alert, allowing the environment team to not only use the platform for exchanging information, but also to store local pictures, laboratory analysis and any other relevant information related to that alert. As a result, our platform can be used as a repository of information from pollution events, while also generating reports with all information to be printed or digitally stored in other systems. Azulfy is currently an Incubatee at ESA Business Incubation Centre in Portugal – IPN, and was awarded with a first round of investments from Portugal Ventures.

Xona Space Systems was founded in 2019 with a mission of supporting modern technology to operate safely in any environment. To that end, Xona is deploying the first commercial satellite navigation infrastructure needed to support intelligent transportation systems like self-driving cars. In the last two decades, satellite navigation has revolutionized many industries. With more than 6.5 billion enabled devices, Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) find utility in nearly all facets of modern life, from the source of time for our communications networks to the source of safety-critical positioning in civil aviation. Now, another revolution is on the horizon, one which promises disruption of transportation, mobility, and safety. 
Autonomous systems in the form of self-driving cars, autonomous aerial platforms, and mobile robotics are on the rise, targeting improved access to the mobility of people, goods, and services. This transformation is one whose complexity demands more than what navigation systems today can provide. Xona Space System’s PULSAR satellite constellation will address this gap by delivering ultra-precise and highly reliable positioning data, essential for the safe and efficient operation of these autonomous systems. By advancing beyond the capabilities of current GNSS technology, Xona's PULSAR system is poised to be a cornerstone in the infrastructure of the emerging era of autonomous transportation, ensuring higher standards of accuracy and reliability in a world moving towards greater automation and connectivity.
To date, Xona US has been the central location for development of the core mission and engineering of the PULSAR system. Xona Canada has established itself as a small centre for R&D and is developing service operations to support critical needs of the service.
Xona UK was incorporated in 2019. Its priority has been as a gateway to business development in the UK. This project serves to springboard Xona UK’s development as a centre for commercialisation-based testing and validation. Eventually it is our goal to host mission operations in the country, splitting the role across continents and mitigating risks to using only a single location. 
Xona Canada was also incorporated in 2019 and hosts the office of the CTO (Tyler Reid). Its operations have focussed on R&D projects such as ionospheric modelling and as a development centre for work in precise point positioning (PPP) and corrections service backend. Work is underway to grow the potential of our Canadian offices to include service operations.

entityDescription:
Mobile Monitoring is a system that combines water and air quality control with smart solutions that facilitate and streamline the analysis of collected data. Our product allows for a quick response to environmental pollution events and minimizes their impact. The Mobile Monitoring System consists of:
- IoT solution along with a monitoring and analytical platform
Devices for continuous monitoring of water parameters, such as: Buoys and measuring floats - control parameters like oxygen content, redox potential, pH, water conductivity, nitrogen, phosphorus, algae, chlorine, which are used as indicators to detect undesirable processes in water. Water buoys for detecting leaks of oil-derived substances. Water drones for precise pollution mapping and creating water quality maps. A mobile device for temporary measurement of water quality. Data from drones and measuring devices are transmitted in real-time to the analytical platform, which controls water parameters and informs about exceedances. The system performs automatic data analysis, notifying users of deviations from the norm, allowing for a quick response and taking action to prevent the spread of pollution or the occurrence of an ecological disaster. Continuous monitoring using measuring devices is crucial because water pollution is often detected too late, with visible consequences. Real-time monitoring is essential, and sometimes even constant monitoring may be insufficient. In cases where minor deviations do not clearly indicate dangerous events or the extent of pollution, water drones provide a two-dimensional water quality map. Mobile Monitoring is a solution for every entity involved in water monitoring. Potential Mobile Monitoring clients include ports, local governments, environmental protection agencies, and industrial plants, who are legally obliged to monitor water quality.

CGIAR is a global research partnership for a food-secure future. CGIAR science is dedicated to transforming food, land, and water systems in a climate crisis. Its research is carried out by 13 CGIAR Centers/Alliances in close collaboration with hundreds of partners, including national and regional research institutes, civil society organizations, academia, development organizations and the private sector.
For 50 years, CGIAR has been a leader in agricultural science and innovation for development. From specific food crops to water systems to policy, CGIAR’s Centers across the globe – working independently and together in partnership – have produced science that has brought benefits to hundreds of millions of the world’s poor.Today, the planet is facing escalating climate and biodiversity crises. Research in agriculture, food, land and water is more multi-disciplinary than ever before. We know much more about the interconnected nature of our food, land and water systems. Traditional funding models have shifted dramatically.The world has changed. And CGIAR is changing with it. CGIAR adopts a holistic view of the food system, from farm to fork, recognizing that many other systems influence it, and that our solutions should minimize trade-offs between increased agricultural productivity and climate and environmental goals.In 2019, CGIAR began a reform to better wield its combined expertise and resources across its Centers.
CGIAR’s Centers are independent legal entities and research organizations collectively home to more than 9,000 scientists, researchers, technicians and staff working in over 80 countries.Each Center has its own local footprint with a host country agreement granting privileges and immunities (including no liabilities for taxes), and each with its own external auditor. Although the Centers draw on the same pooled funding via the CGIAR Trust Fund, and have adopted certain shared policies and procedures, the Centers are governed by their own respective constitutive documents and boards.
The CGIAR System Organization is governed by theCharter of the CGIAR System Organization,and in collaboration with theCGIAR System Council, provides governance to the CGIAR System. The System Organization has an important role in facilitating and overseeing the development, effective and efficient implementation of the2030 Research and Innovation Strategy. The System Organization enters into agreements with the trustee of the CGIAR Trust Fund,Funders, Centers and other relevant entities for funding CGIAR Research and other activities of theCGIAR System.
